ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: the island in the figure is located near about 170°E, 44°S, and as a whole extends in a northeast–southwest direction. Along the coast in the southwestern part of the island there is a relatively large shaded area, and the legend shows that the shading represents "national park"; near this area on the left side of the figure, the words "Fiordland National Park" can be read. Then reason: a fiord is a typical glacial landform formed after a valley formed by glacial erosion is submerged by seawater; the "Fiordland National Park" in the figure is located in the southwestern part of the island, indicating that glacial landforms are significantly developed there. Therefore, the region of the island where glacial landforms are significantly developed is the southwest.
